units.summary: Install the default palette source tables, reset palette upload configuration and select a25-byte palette set. The neighboring reset helper sets eight groups and zero palette offsets.

units.name: ResetPaletteUploadConfig
units.summary: Set eight palette groups, base offset0 and source offset0 for the subsequent NMI upload.

units.name: FadePaletteOut
units.summary: Repeatedly rebuild the adjusted palette and yield a bounded number of frames per step; subtract$10 from the brightness adjustment until the requested limit Y is reached.

units.name: FadePaletteIn
units.summary: Mirror the palette fade loop by adding$10 to the brightness adjustment between timed frame yields. A/X/Y are preserved by the shared rebuild/wait helpers as needed.

units.name: DelayCountdownFrames
units.summary: Wait through the register-preserving frame delay and decrement A until zero. Entry A one through 255 gives a finite countdown; frame yield restores the task selector, while this fixed code remains mapped.

units.name: WaitPaletteFrame
units.summary: Yield a frame, preserve registers around an additional CPU delay and restore them. The adjacent helper disables rendering while preserving universal-color state.

units.name: DisableRendering
units.summary: Clear rendering bits in PPUMASK shadow, temporarily set universal color$0F for a frame, mark palette state negative and restore the saved universal color.

units.name: EnableRendering
units.summary: Set background/sprite render bits in the mask shadow, request palette upload and yield a frame.

units.name: RebuildPalettePreservingRegisters
units.summary: Save A/X/Y, rebuild the brightness-adjusted palette, then restore Y/X/A and return. Callers retain their fade-loop registers.

units.name: LoadPaletteSet
units.summary: Compute sourceBase+24*A, copy25 bytes into the source palette buffer and rebuild the adjusted palette. The overlap between adjacent sets is preserved.

units.name: CopyPaletteFragment
units.summary: Set the fragment count/destination offset and select the auxiliary palette table before the shared buffer copy.

units.name: CopyPaletteBytes
units.summary: Copy A bytes from (scratch pointer),Y to the palette source buffer at X. Y/X advance; the count is consumed.

units.name: SetBrightnessAndContinue
units.summary: Store supplied brightness and enter the native palette brightness loop. Entry requires X count one through twenty-five and Y within zero through twenty-four, matching the initialized loop interface; this is a subentry rather than the ordinary initialization prefix.

units.name: ApplyPaletteBrightness
units.summary: For25 palette bytes, retain high-bit sentinel colors, normalize$0F, add the brightness adjustment and clamp invalid/dark colors. Mask output to six bits and request an NMI upload.

units.name: QueuePpuRecords
units.summary: Select the source bank from RAM4F, then copy PPU address high/low, packed count/stride and count-plus-one payload bytes into the immediate queue untilFF. This helper leaves the selected lower bank in place; it does not restore task selector85. Inventory and credits callers establish4F=4 and6 respectively.

units.name: QueuePpuRecordsAtAddress
units.summary: Select source bank RAM4F and copy packed PPU records using the scratch-supplied destination. The selected lower bank remains after return; resource selector50 belongs to tile upload and does not establish this text bank.

units.name: QueueTileTransfer
units.summary: Append one six-byte transfer descriptor only while the12-byte queue has room. Pack the tile destination and nametable bits; retain source pointer, row count and row width for vblank consumption.

units.name: FlushTileTransfers
units.summary: Defer when a scrolling-column upload is pending. Otherwise select the transfer source bank, process descriptors in six-byte steps, restore task bank and clear queue length.

units.name: UploadTileTransfer
units.summary: Stream row-width bytes through PPUDATA, advance the source pointer per row and repeat rowCount+1 times. Width8 pads with eight zero bytes before the next row.

units.name: PadHalfTileTransfer
units.summary: Write eight zero bytes between eight-byte source rows to form a full16-byte pattern row in PPU memory.

units.name: NextTileTransfer
units.summary: Advance the descriptor index by six and continue the bounded queue flush.

units.name: UpdateSceneController
units.summary: Scene numbers below four use initialization and the common scene dispatcher. Higher scenes consume a scene request through the separate presentation path. The index1 input-selection handler supports an ordinary return; other targets retain separate stack contracts.

units.name: InitializeSceneState
units.summary: Clear scene request, initialize the common display/actors, set scene mode4 and allocate task class3. This supported static transition is distinct from natural victory.

units.name: ConsumeSceneRequest
units.summary: For a pending request, stop gameplay tasks, silence sound and dialog, wait through the request-specific presentation, initialize scene display and task4, choose the next scene setup index and clear request/mode. Natural boss completion remains unresolved.

units.name: InitializeSceneDisplay
units.summary: Disable drawing, clear scroll/split state, initialize display flags and sprite resources, and configure the actor draw interval. The following dispatcher loads a six-byte scene setup record and an RTS-encoded target.

units.name: DispatchSceneSetup
units.summary: Multiply the scene index by six, load background/palette/music-like setup fields, yield, then push an RTS-encoded scene target. Natural activation of every scene is unproved.

units.name: SeedTitleRandomState
units.summary: Seed eight random bytes with$5B, save task bank and temporarily select bank4 before entering the title presentation.

units.name: EnterTitlePresentation
units.summary: Call the bank4 title routine with a saved task selector, restore that selector from the stack and mapper, clear actors/progress and branch into password setup when the title choice requests it. Finish with fade/sound cleanup.

units.name: RunSceneInputSelection
units.summary: Clear actors and fade in, yield frames until one of the two high controller bits chooses scene index3 or2, then fade out and return.

units.name: EnterPasswordInputScene
units.summary: Set next setup index3, select bank5 and call its native password-input routine. The following gameplay initialization is a separate scene target.

units.name: InitializeGameplayScene
units.summary: Initialize scene3, load its graphics and episode selection screen, reset gameplay state and accept Start. Then select the episode room/camera record and load its room resources. A controller-two chord permits episode cycling on the selection screen.

units.name: RestorePlayerAfterSceneActors
units.summary: After the native episode actor script returns, restore saved player world coordinates, height and episode room. Entry has task selector six and lower selector six; the fixed continuation itself performs no lower-window read. The selected script cleanup supplies the local balanced return contract.

units.name: SelectControllerTwoEpisodeRecord
units.summary: Initialize a selection index, wait for controller-two input and either advance the index or apply a four-byte episode/room/progress record. Supported record indices are zero through four; the loop does not itself prove a global maximum. This is a separate entry after the preceding RTS, with natural use unresolved.

units.name: ReadControllerEpisodeChoice
units.summary: Wait for controller-one input, convert the low nibble into an episode choice and return. Controller field and frame-wait mechanics are established; original debug/menu entry remains uncertain.

units.name: InitializeEpisodeClearScene
units.summary: Initialize scene4 and its flags, run the bank4 episode-clear dialog route, then draw the episode result, wait for input and run the decimal progress/counter presentation. Artificial routes establish presentation but not natural boss victory.

units.name: ContinueEpisodeProgressPresentation
units.summary: After progress presentation, queue text, wait for input and advance episode. Request scene six at the final episode or perform the other presentation cleanup, explicitly select bank five for password display and finish the fade/wait sequence. Entry requires task selector and text resource selector four; fixed continuations survive lower-bank changes. Natural boss victory and all-input termination remain unproved.

units.name: InitializeSceneSixPalette
units.summary: Run scene6 palette/ending setup under a saved task selector, restore it, then present a timed button-pattern gate. The completed pattern sets task selector6 and enters the bank6 credits/sound-selection routine.

units.name: RestoreEndingCallerTaskSelector
units.summary: Pop the caller selector saved before selecting task bank six and calling the ending montage, then join the native bank-selection continuation. The saved byte must survive the montage's established stack/scene contract; its numeric value is not assumed.

units.name: ResumeAfterCredits
units.summary: After the native credits return, jump to the fixed scene continuation. The lower mapping after credits is irrelevant here; this does not claim that every sound-menu input returns. The following isolated return byte remains unknown.

units.name: InitializeSceneFive
units.summary: Clear four scene-local bytes, initialize scene5, show its timed input-gated presentation, clear the five persistent progress bytes and initialize the game clock. Exact narrative meaning remains tentative.

units.name: ContinueSceneFiveInitialization
units.summary: Continue clearing scene-local bytes across the physical8KiB boundary, then initialize the scene and its timed presentation.

units.name: DeactivateAllActors
units.summary: Clear the96-byte actor array through a byte-indexed loop. This resets all eight twelve-byte records, including field tails.

units.name: RunSceneProgressPresentation
units.summary: Load presentation graphics, reset local counters and derive the displayed decimal progress fields from persistent progress. Queue text and yield between visible updates; narrative purpose is tentative.

units.name: AddPresentationProgressDigits
units.summary: Choose a five-digit increment vector from A, add into persistent decimal digits with carry and saturate all five digits to9 on overflow. Redraw the resulting number through the common digit writer.

units.name: DrawPersistentProgressDigits
units.summary: Write five decimal tiles in reverse field order to consecutive PPU cells, append a zero digit and yield a frame.

units.name: SaturateProgressDigits
units.summary: Set all five persistent decimal progress fields to9; the caller uses this on decimal carry overflow.

units.name: DrawPresentationHealthUnits
units.summary: Render paired units with full, half and blank tiles from the supplied count. The original health bound determines row width; each tile advances the16-bit PPU position.

units.name: ConsumeFirstPresentationCounter
units.summary: Yield, decrement the first item counter until negative, add its progress vector, redraw its digit and wait12 frames per unit.

units.name: ConsumeSecondPresentationCounter
units.summary: Apply the same presentation loop to the second item counter, with its own PPU cell and the shared progress increment.

units.name: DecrementPresentationDigits
units.summary: Subtract one across the local decimal digits with borrow, then redraw the five-digit display. This loop feeds the gradual progress accumulation presentation.

units.name: DrawSceneProgressDigits
units.summary: Read five local numeric fields in reverse order, add digit tile base$DA and queue consecutive PPU tiles, then append a zero digit and yield.

units.name: InitializeRoomGameplay
units.summary: If room initialization is complete enter the frame update. Otherwise create the player task, install follower resources, initialize HUD/clock/health presentation and load room-specific pointers before joining common room setup.

units.name: InitializeCurrentRoom
units.summary: Allocate the player task, mark follower type visible, load room descriptor and three transfer lists, select background bank, clamp initial camera from player spawn and load room pointers before frame processing.

units.name: RestoreRoomDisplayAfterActors
units.summary: Restore the saved actor-task offset, select the task bank, enable rendering, refresh actor coordinates, fade and enable tasks before saving frame phase. The matched stack partner precedes player/follower initialization; supported initially inactive records supply local returns, not a universal actor-return contract.

units.name: PlayEpisodeSoundRange
units.summary: Index episode-specific sound ID/count pairs, retain the starting ID and call the bank-restoring consecutive-sound wrapper.

units.name: LoadCurrentRoomPointers
units.summary: Resolve episode/room block, layout, metatile and attribute pointers from banked directories. Select resource bank5 for the native room actor setup helper; return continuation uses the established task bank contract.

units.name: UpdateGameplayFrame
units.summary: Choose a recovery pose when the recovery timer alternates, update environment graphics, scrolling, actor triggers/collisions and dialog/inventory state. Restore the intended task bank around banked calls.

units.name: UpdateGameplayEnvironment
units.summary: Pass the camera movement request to scrolling, update actor screen coordinates, activate room/column triggers and run the banked spawner. Update follower/ambient logic before selecting the inventory bank.

units.name: UpdateGameplayInterface
units.summary: Check inventory entry, timed interaction messages and scene-completion conditions. Low health can periodically request a sound. Compare episode completion progress to select a mode flag.

units.name: AdjustProgressFromControllerTwo
units.summary: Derive a delta from controller-two bits $0C: one direction gives minus one, the other plus one, and both together give three, preserve it on the stack and update progress fields. Derive a HUD tile from the adjusted value and queue it through the fixed tile helper with initialized scratch arguments. Mechanically a controller/state/HUD helper; original debug intent and natural entry are tentative.

units.name: TriggerControllerTwoDebugAction
units.summary: When controller-two bit seven is set, call the fixed action helper with scratch selector $C8 and increment that selector. Otherwise return unchanged. No original natural entry is established.

units.name: ScrollRoom
units.summary: Select the background bank, add/subtract the movement request according to direction, clamp at world bounds and update new16-pixel columns when the camera crosses a boundary.

units.name: ScrollCameraRight
units.summary: Add the requested step to camera low X, carrying into its page and clamping at the room width.

units.name: ScrollCameraLeft
units.summary: Subtract the requested step with borrow; clamp at the left edge before the shared column test.

units.name: CheckScrollColumnBoundary
units.summary: Compare current and previous scroll bit4. On a crossing, rebuild tile/attribute staging and mark room graphics pending, then restore the task bank.

units.name: FinishRoomScroll
units.summary: Use camera page parity for the nametable selection and restore the current task bank.

units.name: PrepareScrollUpload
units.summary: Build the destination tile column, nametable high byte and pending-column flags from camera position and direction. A companion helper resolves20-byte block descriptions from the room layout.

units.name: ResolveRoomColumn
units.summary: Select a room-layout index and multiply the block ID by20, then add the block-data base to obtain a20-byte column descriptor.

units.name: BuildScrollColumn
units.summary: Resolve the column and its attributes, then expand ten metatile IDs into two20-byte tile columns in the staging buffer. Restore the task bank afterward.

units.name: ExpandMetatileColumn
units.summary: Copy four tile IDs from the metatile definition into the two staged20-byte columns, advancing the output index twice.

units.name: ResolveRoomLayout
units.summary: Combine scroll direction, camera page and layout offset to resolve the16-byte room layout page pointer; preserve exact high-bit arithmetic.

units.name: BuildScrollAttributes
units.summary: When the pending flag requires it, resolve the five-byte attribute record, compute the destination attribute offset and copy its bytes into staging.

units.name: ResolveAttributeRecord
units.summary: Multiply a room-layout attribute ID by five and add the attribute-data base to obtain a record pointer.

units.name: ResolveMetatileDefinition
units.summary: Multiply the metatile ID by four and add its definition base; the result points to four tile IDs.

units.name: MultiplyByTwenty
units.summary: Compute the16-bit product A*20 using saved A*4 plus A*16. Return low byte in A and scratch$40, high byte in scratch$41.

units.name: PrimeRoomScrollColumns
units.summary: Under native room/spawn setup, start camera32 units before spawn and emit36 column updates. Initialize each tile batch, refresh screen coordinates, update bank6 actor triggers when required and yield every eight columns. Clear pending direction/step and restore task selector85 at completion.

units.name: RestoreTaskBankAfterRoomTriggers
units.summary: Reload task selector $85 and remap after the room-trigger calls. A no-match trigger or full actor slots provides an ordinary local return; arbitrary actor callbacks are not covered.

units.name: LoadBackgroundPalette
units.summary: Mask the selection to seven bits, multiply by13 and select a13-byte palette fragment at the fixed source table. Copy to palette buffer offset0.

units.name: LoadSpritePalette
units.summary: Mask selection, multiply by12 and select a12-byte fragment. Copy to palette buffer offset13.

units.name: LoadRoomDescriptor
units.summary: Index a four-byte room record through the episode directory. Load world width and background bank, then select background and sprite palettes from the final two fields. Episode counts17/24/27/36 are independently bounded by pointer origins and the next native routine.

units.name: LoadRoomTransferSelectors
units.summary: Compute room*3 in the episode selector stream, invoke the tile-transfer loader for each of three IDs and restore the index after each call. Descriptor counts match the room records17/24/27/36.

units.name: InitializeCameraFromSpawn
units.summary: For an interior player spawn center camera128 units behind it; at room edges keep camera at the bounded edge. Copy spawn world X to player and set camera page/low consistently.

units.name: PlayCurrentRoomEntrySound
units.summary: Resolve the episode room-sound byte table, index by room and pass that ID to the task-bank-restoring sound wrapper.

units.name: CheckRoomSoundTrigger
units.summary: Scan three-byte room/sound/count records to a negative room terminator. On a room match silence current sound, retain its ID and start the indexed sound range. Natural trigger occurrence is separate from this format contract.

units.name: UpdateRoomAnimatedTiles
units.summary: Select an episode/room effect index; high-bit entries disable updates. Otherwise enter the shared animated-tile descriptor consumer.

units.name: QueueAnimatedTileFrame
units.summary: Select an effect descriptor, tick an interval at a four-frame cadence and select a source frame. Descriptor fields supply destination, size and source bank; enqueue the transfer through the bounded two-record queue.

units.name: QueueSinglePpuTile
units.summary: Append one PPU destination and one tile byte with count-minus-one0. The following entry checks health/time and dispatches episode completion tests.

units.name: CheckEpisodeCompletion
units.summary: Zero health or zero minutes/seconds requests scene4 with reason2. Otherwise jump through the episode-specific completion test; request reason1 marks the supported completion condition.

units.name: CheckEpisodeOneCompletion
units.summary: Require progress count at least7, both characters in room0/page0 and camera X0, then request scene4/reason1.

units.name: CheckEpisodeTwoCompletion
units.summary: Require progress count at least9 before the common position-dependent completion path. Other episodes retain their own predicates.

units.name: RequestSceneFour
units.summary: Set scene mode four and scene request one, matching adjacent episode completion setters, then return. The exact field interface is established; no natural callback selection is claimed.

units.name: CheckEpisodeThreeCompletion
units.summary: Require progress-related counter039C exactly5 before requesting scene4 with completion reason1. This is the third episode predicate, separate from the >=12 fourth-episode rule.

units.name: CheckLaterEpisodeCompletion
units.summary: Require progress count at least12, then request scene4/reason1. This request alone does not establish scene-controller activation.

units.name: UpdateFollowerTimerMode
units.summary: Defer during palette fade or special player state. Save normal timer fields while follower is absent; on reappearance clear the mode and restore saved seconds/minutes/subseconds.

units.name: GateFollowerTimerMode
units.summary: Check the player state low bit and a saved-mode flag before deciding whether to start or stop the temporary follower-related timer.

units.name: StartFollowerTimerMode
units.summary: Save minutes/seconds/subseconds, then install minutes1/seconds59/subseconds59. Reappearance clears the mode flag and calls a message helper.

units.name: RestoreNormalGameClock
units.summary: Restore seconds/minutes/subseconds from the saved follower-timer fields, then return.

units.name: UpdateActorScreenCoordinates
units.summary: For eight12-byte actor records, compute screen X from world X minus camera and mark on-screen type bit7 only when the high difference is zero. Hide the follower when rooms differ.

units.name: ClearActorRecordAndContinue
units.summary: Clear the selected actor's eleven fields, preserving the repeated first store exactly, then join the native stride-twelve continuation. Entry Y is a record offset zero through eighty-four in multiples of twelve and X is one through eight records remaining.

units.name: ProbeFollowerRoomTiles
units.summary: Copy follower-room layout/metatile pointers into the shared collision context, then use the common directional probe dispatcher.

units.name: ProbePlayerRoomTiles
units.summary: Copy current-room layout/metatile pointers into the shared collision context, then select the requested probe direction. Y is the direction selector and X the actor offset.

units.name: DispatchTileProbe
units.summary: Preserve direction Y across the background-bank switch and jump through a word table. Restoring the task bank is the responsibility of the concrete probe paths.

units.name: ProbeActorTop
units.summary: Set sample Y to actor Y minus half-height, then use the common three horizontal sample probe and task-bank restoration path.

units.name: ProbeActorHorizontalSamples
units.summary: For a fixed vertical sample, test left/center/right world-X points spanning the actor half-width. Stop at the first solid result, preserve it across task-bank restoration and return.

units.name: ProbeActorBottom
units.summary: Set the vertical sample to actor Y+half-height and reuse the three-point horizontal test. The adjacent left-edge path tests top/bottom at X-half-width.

units.name: ProbeActorLeft
units.summary: At world X minus half-width, test the two vertical extrema; restore the task bank and return the first nonzero solid result.

units.name: ProbeActorRight
units.summary: At world X plus half-width, test top and bottom extrema and preserve the solid result across task-bank restoration.

units.name: ReadCollisionTile
units.summary: Resolve a world coordinate through room layout,20-byte block data and four-tile metatile definitions. Select the quadrant from low coordinate bits and return solid for tile IDs at or above$60; retain the raw tile in scratch.

units.name: ReturnSolidTile
units.summary: Return A=1 for tile IDs$60 and above; the adjacent clear path returns0.

units.name: FindPlayerSupport
units.summary: Load the player world coordinate/height and scan supporting records through the shared support finder.

units.name: FindFollowerSupport
units.summary: Load the follower world coordinate/height and scan supporting records with actor offset12.

units.name: FindActorSupport
units.summary: Load the selected actor world position and height, then call the shared support finder; return its carry and Y result.

units.name: PropagateActorTypeOnOverlap
units.summary: Test the actor against player and follower. On overlap merge its low-seven-bit type into the character type/visibility field; advance Y by actor stride12 through the two records.

units.name: ScanDynamicActorRecords
units.summary: Save caller X in scratch and start the actor scan at offset $18. With carry clear on entry, return the first negative active record with carry clear; exhaustion returns carry set. Natural caller and original selection purpose remain unresolved.

units.name: ScanLaterActorRecords
units.summary: Start the same record scan at offset $30. Advance by twelve through $54, returning the first negative active record under the carry-clear entry contract, or carry set after offset $60. The eight-record layout bounds the scan.

units.name: IncreaseHealth
units.summary: Increase health up to20, choose the correct half-cell HUD tile from the previous parity and join the common health display update. Undo increments beyond the cap.

units.name: DecreaseHealth
units.summary: Decrement health but prevent underflow, request a warning sound below2 and queue the relevant half-byte health display update. The exact tile packing is retained.

units.name: InitializeGameClock
units.summary: Load episode-specific minutes, set seconds/subseconds59, save the same values for temporary follower mode and queue the timer display.

units.name: TickGameClock
units.summary: Decrement frame/subsecond, seconds and minutes with59 reloads; below zero freeze subseconds at$FF and zero displayed time. Queue decimal digits for the timer HUD.

units.name: QueueGameClockDigits
units.summary: Convert minutes and seconds to tens/ones, map digits to tile codes from$DA and append an eight-byte PPU update record including the separator tile.

units.name: SplitDecimalDigits
units.summary: Repeatedly subtract10 to obtain ones in scratch$18 and tens in scratch$19. Input is the bounded HUD value; no general BCD assumption.

units.name: UpdatePeriodicInterface
units.summary: If dialog mode is active, update dialog; for scene4 and above tick the game clock. Scene numbering is a state-machine value rather than a direct ending flag.

units.name: SelectDialogWindow
units.summary: Select one of two eight-byte window configurations and copy its PPU bounds/prompt fields into dialog state. Alternate entry selects the second configuration.

units.name: RequestDialogIfIdle
units.summary: Reject a nonnegative request while dialog is active. Otherwise select dialogue bank2, read the indexed word pointer, restore task bank and mark the asynchronous dialog active.

units.name: RunBlockingDialog
units.summary: Load the indexed dialogue pointer from bank2, restore task bank, start dialog with state$21 and sound, then save/freeze the game timer while the shared wait loop runs. Its suffix restores the saved timer byte.

units.name: WaitForDialogCompletion
units.summary: Yield palette/frame work, allow the action press to hurry dialog, and loop while its state is active. Restore the previously stacked timer byte on exit.

units.name: LoadTileTransferList
units.summary: Index a descriptor list, read its count and seven fields per transfer, enqueue each bounded transfer and yield before the next. Preserve the source descriptor index across the loop.

units.name: TestGroundedActorOverlap
units.summary: Require actor Y equal saved ground Y before entering the ordinary screen overlap test; airborne actors return carry set.

units.name: TestActorScreenOverlap
units.summary: Require both records active/visible, take absolute height/screen-X deltas and compare against summed half-extents. Carry clear means overlap; carry set means separated/inactive. Edge equality is treated as separated.

units.name: FindSupportingActor
units.summary: Scan records$30..$54 at stride12 and test active candidates. Return the first overlapping Y with carry clear; exhausting the range returns Y=$60 with carry set.

units.name: TestActorWorldOverlap
units.summary: Compare height delta and16-bit world-X separation against summed half-extents. Preserve the stacked low difference through high-byte sign handling; carry clear means overlap.

units.name: UpdateAmbientMessageTimer
units.summary: Skip episode-specific excluded rooms, advance a120-by8 timer and occasionally choose a message from pseudo-random state when dialog is idle. Choice depends on follower visibility.

units.name: TickAmbientMessageTimer
units.summary: Increment the short timer to120, then increment its long counter; at8 reset it and choose a message only if no dialog is active.

units.name: RequestFrameSelectedMessage
units.summary: Derive one of two message IDs from frame bits and request it only through the shared idle-dialog gate.

units.name: SelectPhasedDialogMessage
units.summary: Use frame phase modulo four to choose message $25 through $28 and call the established dialog helper. Busy dialog can return directly; text startup restores the task selector. Natural message selection remains unresolved.

units.name: CheckFollowerNearbyObjects
units.summary: Skip excluded rooms and invisible follower. Scan support records and compare world-X displacement to facing-specific thresholds$50/$B0; a match requests a message selected from frame phase.

units.name: UpdateDialog
units.summary: Defer while transfers or scrolling uploads are pending. Initialize dialog window state or continue its pacing, parsing, line wrapping, prompt and clearing paths. State bits coordinate asynchronous PPU row uploads.

units.name: InitializeDialogWindow
units.summary: Mark initialization complete, copy the destination address, clear cursor/buffer/parser state and request a window redraw before continuing.

units.name: DispatchDialogState
units.summary: State bits choose pending prompt, completion, row upload or character pacing. A delayed end marker sets a completion timeout rather than consuming a printable tile.

units.name: TickDialogCharacterDelay
units.summary: Wait the per-character counter, then fetch tokens until a printable/control token is obtained. $FF starts a50-tick completion wait; $B0..$BF changes character delay.

units.name: AdvanceDialogLine
units.summary: Advance PPU destination by32 and circular buffer row by21. End-line markers or the width20 limit enter wrapping/prompt logic.

units.name: WaitDialogPrompt
units.summary: Use the prompt helper result to retain/clear the wait state. Carry set keeps the dialog suspended for input.

units.name: EmitDialogCharacter
units.summary: Queue and buffer a character, increment column and adjust the temporary row/address cursor. At column20 enter line wrap; end markers can terminate earlier.

units.name: WrapDialogLine
units.summary: Wrap the21-byte circular row index within168 bytes, compare against the window end address and possibly wait for prompt input before advancing to the next line.

units.name: MarkDialogPromptWait
units.summary: Set dialog state bit7 and reset its PPU destination to the configured prompt/window position before joining the row-clearing path.

units.name: ClearNextDialogRows
units.summary: Compute next destination row and reset column, then clear42 bytes covering two circular-buffer rows.

units.name: UploadDialogRows
units.summary: Point the row-upload source at the circular buffer, configure a four-row upload and wrap the source buffer when it reaches$045C. On completion clear the upload state and schedule the fixed terminator rows.

units.name: QueueDialogCharacter
units.summary: Store A in the circular text buffer and append one PPU tile update at the current dialog address. The neighboring HUD helper uses X/Y directly as its PPU destination.

units.name: QueueHudTile
units.summary: Append destination high/low, count0 and tile A, followed by$FF sentinel; update the queue length and return carry clear.

units.name: HurryDialog
units.summary: If dialog is active, replace its state with the fast row-upload/clear state, hide its prompt sprite and return carry set.

units.name: ClearDialogWindow
units.summary: Initialize/continue the window clearing state, upload four21-byte rows and clear its high state bit when finished. The adjacent row initializer installs source width21.

units.name: InitializeDialogRowUpload
units.summary: Copy window base PPU destination and set row width21 and row count4 for the NMI upload helper.

units.name: ReadDialogToken
units.summary: Read the pointer-stack stream. $FF pops; $FD/$FB select pointer-control forms and $FA shares the jump path. Indexed substitution selects a pointer from the fixed directory; plain tokens advance the stream and return in scratch.

units.name: ReadDialogPointerControl
units.summary: Handle indexed pointer control through the banked table, otherwise advance the pointer by one. The push helper saves a two-byte continuation and increments nesting depth.

units.name: PushDialogPointer
units.summary: Store stream+2 in the current pointer slot, carry into its high byte, then advance the two-byte slot index and parser depth.

units.name: UpdateDialogPrompt
units.summary: When the prompt bit is enabled, install its sprite tile/position and blink every eight ticks until held A-like input is detected. Return carry set while waiting, clear on dismissal.

units.name: Reset
units.summary: Disable interrupts/decimal mode, initialize the stack/PPU, wait two vblanks and clear internal RAM. Write mapper initialization, copy the RAM hardware-store stub, initialize display/APU and allocate the initial scheduler task.

units.name: RunTaskScheduler
units.summary: Scan five16-byte task slots beginning$92. Active bit7 admits a slot; decrement its delay or select its bank/handler. Actor offset is slot*12, separate from task stride16. Yield a frame after the fifth slot.

units.name: ContinueDelayedTaskScan
units.summary: After the native task countdown decrement, jump back into the delayed-task scan. Fixed mapping is sufficient here; no caller or lower-bank preservation premise is needed.

units.name: DispatchScheduledTask
units.summary: Pair the five handler targets with selectors4,4,6,6,6, write the selected value to RAM85 and the mapper, then tail-jump to the handler. Player/follower tasks therefore use physical banks8/9 and actor tasks12/13; all share fixed banks14/15. Natural task/actor selection is separate.

units.name: CallScheduledHandler
units.summary: Load the selected handler pointer and jump indirectly. The adjacent scheduler end yields once and restarts the five-slot scan.

units.name: AllocateTask
units.summary: Search a bounded allocation class for a free16-byte task slot, mark it active, copy the two initial state bytes and clear its delay/state tail. Return carry set when exhausted and carry clear with allocated selector in A on success.

units.name: DisableTask
units.summary: Save A/X/Y, convert A to a16-byte task offset and clear its active flag, then restore all three registers and return.

units.name: WaitFrames
units.summary: Yield through the common frame helper and decrement A until zero. Callers use a bounded nonzero frame count; zero would wrap for256 yields.

units.name: Nmi
units.summary: Preserve registers, disable rendering/NMI in the shadows, DMA OAM page2, flush queued transfers/PPU work and palette/scroll updates, then signal the frame-ready byte before restoring registers and RTI.

units.name: NmiFlushQueues
units.summary: Flush nametable fill, immediate PPU records and pending tile rows before the column/palette updates.

units.name: NmiRestoreDisplay
units.summary: Upload scrolling columns, deferred resource streams and palette; restore nametable selection, mask and scroll, set frame-ready and restore A/X/Y before RTI.

units.name: InitializePpuShadows
units.summary: Initialize control/mask shadows and zero scroll. The adjacent vblank helper waits for a new vblank edge rather than returning during an existing one.

units.name: WaitNewVblank
units.summary: Poll until the current vblank ends, then wait for the next rising vblank status bit.

units.name: ClearBothNametables
units.summary: Choose fill tile$FC and request fills of nametables$20/$24 on successive frame yields while rendering is disabled; restore the mask shadow afterward.

units.name: FillRequestedNametable
units.summary: If requested, clear the request and write960 fill tiles plus64 zero attribute bytes at the selected nametable. PPUDATA increment is forced horizontal.

units.name: QueueDeferredPpuStream
units.summary: Append a source pointer to the deferred stream queue only below its$A0 capacity threshold. The queue shares backing storage with immediate records; scheduling governs ownership.

units.name: FlushDeferredPpuStreams
units.summary: Select the deferred resource bank, decode each queued pointer stream, then restore RAM85 task bank and clear queue length. The decoder uses conventional balanced recursive stream calls.

units.name: BeginPpuStream
units.summary: Initialize stream index Y=0 before the recursive PPU command decoder.

units.name: DecodePpuStream
units.summary: Read signed-leading commands: $FF returns; other negative leads recurse through pointer streams. Save pointer high/low/Y and restore Y/low/high at FC3C. Positive commands select destination and inline or indirect payload.

units.name: RestoreParentPpuStream
units.summary: Pop Y and pointer low/high after a nested PPU command stream, then resume the parent decoder. The three pops balance its saved stream state.

units.name: DecodePpuStreamDestination
units.summary: Take the low six command bits as PPU high address, read low address and branch between inline payload and an indirect source pointer.

units.name: DecodeIndirectPpuPayload
units.summary: Save stream pointer/index, load an indirect payload pointer and decode it, restore the original stream, then continue. The adjacent payload decoder handles length/stride/repeat bits.

units.name: DecodePpuPayload
units.summary: Low five bits encode count-minus-one. High flags choose horizontal/vertical increment and repeated/literal bytes; optional row controls add a row count/stride. Configure PPU control accordingly.

units.name: WritePpuPayload
units.summary: Set destination, write the count bytes with literal/repeat semantics, advance source and destination for each row, then return to stream decoding. Preserve encoded operand widths throughout.

units.name: UploadScrollColumn
units.summary: When pending, stream the staged pair of20-byte tile columns vertically. Optionally upload five attribute bytes at eight-byte destination increments, then clear the pending flag.

units.name: CheckPaletteUpload
units.summary: Return from scroll upload; the adjacent palette path skips negative/zero request state and writes the adjusted palette only when requested.

units.name: UploadPalette
units.summary: Set palette destination, emit universal color plus three colors per group, clear request and reset the PPU address latch. Palette state controls count/source offset independently of source classification.

units.name: FlushImmediatePpuQueue
units.summary: Skip empty queue or incompatible palette state. Decode address, packed increment/count and count-plus-one payload, write through PPUDATA and clear queue length at completion.

units.name: WriteImmediatePpuRecord
units.summary: Install the increment mode, write the record payload, then loop to the next record until the queue index reaches length.

units.name: DrawSingleSprite
units.summary: Set one-sprite count and neutral attributes, preserve caller Y and invoke the shared sprite part emitter.

units.name: DrawSingleSpriteWithZeroAttributes
units.summary: Save supplied allocator index A, clear sprite attributes, restore the allocator and enter the native single-part sprite emitter. Balanced stack prefix matches the existing sprite interface; no caller-Y preservation or natural entry is claimed.

units.name: EmitOneSpritePart
units.summary: Preserve X, set count1 and call the common emitter using the supplied sprite stream pointer/position.

units.name: DrawSpritePartsWithZeroAttributes
units.summary: Save allocator index A, clear attributes and restore the allocator before the native multi-part emitter. This balanced prefix uses the established allocator/attribute fields; actual caller remains unknown.

units.name: EmitSpriteParts
units.summary: Index OAM by four times the allocator. Transform relative Y/X by attribute flip flags, clip wrapped horizontal positions by hiding Y, write tile/attributes and advance stream and allocator. Count controls the loop.

units.name: WriteSpritePosition
units.summary: Add transformed offsets to screen origin, subtract1 from OAM Y, detect horizontal sign/wrap crossing and hide clipped sprites. Then write tile and XOR-composed attributes.

units.name: WriteSpriteTileAttributes
units.summary: Store X/tile/attributes in OAM, advance the resource stream and sprite allocator, and repeat until the part count reaches zero.

units.name: HideSpritesFromIndex
units.summary: Set the allocator from A, then reuse the common hide loop.

units.name: HideRemainingSprites
units.summary: For the requested count, set OAM Y=$F0 and advance the allocator, preserving caller X. Other OAM fields need no clearing for hidden sprites.

units.name: HideSpriteSlot
units.summary: Preserve X, multiply sprite index A by4 and set only its OAM Y byte toF0. Restore caller X and return.

units.name: HideAllSprites
units.summary: Hide64 sprites starting at index0 and yield a frame so the DMA copy reaches OAM.

units.name: SelectSoundBankForSilence
units.summary: Use fixed identity-table byte3 to select sound bank3 with a bus-conflict-safe mapper write. The accepted suffix silences channels and restores the task bank.

units.name: PlaySound
units.summary: Preserve sound ID, select bank3 and call the single-sequence initializer. Restore the scheduler bank afterward; this fixed-bank wrapper does not promise general bank preservation across arbitrary calls.

units.name: StartSoundAndRestoreBank
units.summary: Call the banked initializer with the saved sound ID, then restore the task bank through the mapper selector table.

units.name: PlaySoundRange
units.summary: Preserve starting sound ID and count, select sound bank3 and call the consecutive-sequence initializer. Restore RAM85 task bank afterward, rather than promising preservation of an arbitrary incoming switch bank.

units.name: SelectPrgBank
units.summary: Use A as the selector, load an identical byte from the fixed identity table and write it to the same mapper address. This bus-conflict-safe write selects a16KiB UxROM bank; selector values are not physical8KiB bank indices.

units.name: ReturnAfterPrgSelection
units.summary: Return after the mapper write. The following selector table is classified data, separated from this code.

units.name: DrawActorPoseFromA
units.summary: Store A as the pose offset, then enter DrawActorPose, which establishes its own resource pointers and preserves X/Y. Y is a valid actor offset and actor resource group must be initialized; native D7FC supplies the same argument through scratch27. Natural selection of this alternate entry is unknown.

units.name: ReturnFromSceneInputSelection
units.summary: Return after the supported scene setup index1 handler. The dispatcher consumes its synthetic return pair; the ordinary input-selection handler preserves this caller pair under its initialized frame/fade and finite input-exit contract. Other scene handlers need separate contracts.

units.name: ReturnFromValidPasswordScene
units.summary: Return after an encoder-compatible password succeeds through the native bank5 input/decoder path. B454 queues digit tiles and yields with task selector5; it does not write $01FF,X or remove a return pair. Arbitrary password paths are not claimed to return.

units.name: TransformArithmeticScratchPair
units.summary: Transform A and arithmetic scratch high:low ($41:$40), then return A=low. With initial a,m=low,h=high, t=((4*a mod256)+m+((a>>6)&1)) mod256; result=4*((h<<8)|t) mod65536. Incoming carry and ADC carry are overwritten by shifts. The shared paired carry/output interface is established; intended argument relation and game purpose remain unknown. Do not assume a general multiply-by-twenty entry.

units.name: TickDialogCompletionTimeout
units.summary: If dialog_character_timer is nonzero, enter its native decrement/return path; zero enters cleanup, redraw and palette-frame wait. The FF-token producer seeds this same timer with $32 (50 ticks). Requires initialized dialog/frame state; the current dispatcher bypasses this alternate entry and its natural selector is unknown.

units.name: InstallSpriteZeroMarkerAt189
units.summary: Install sprite-zero marker at Y=189 by supplying the complete A argument to InstallSpriteZeroMarker. The shared body sets X=$FC, tile=$7E and attributes=$20, then returns normally. Requires the same OAM initialization as the native A-taking entry; fixed banks14/15 suffice, lower banks are irrelevant. Natural callers and scene timing are unknown; 189 is a literal parameter, not an established scene default.
